original.description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected.  User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Server in Space (SiS) module for regenerative processors in satellite communication systems, enablingefficienton-board data processing and offering advanced autonomy applications andemergency management services.TargetedImprovements: Enabling application layer processing on-board for Servers in Space to offer advanced autonomy applications and emergency management services.Description: It is expected that satellites will have a larger percentage of regenerative processing, which opens the door to application layer processing on-board of satellites. The mainchallenge to be addressed is the availability of a Server in Space (SiS) with application layer processing, with technical challenges to be addressed in terms of powerconsumption, radiation hardening of ground-based data centre technology, and maturity of application layersoftware for embedded devices. Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. Recent advancements of cloud providers in embedded processors, as well as technical developments inefficient FPGAs and computational memories, allow to link this concept to 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) and Direct-to-Device (D2D) connectivity, enabling thesatellite to act as a server in space. By integrating the application layer on the satellite, cloud services, currently only provided on ground, could be made available to users innatural disaster situations or with special requirements that cannot use the regular network, e.g. very stringent latency needs like Internet-of-Things (IoT) or autonomousdriving.This activity will design and develop a cloud computing module, integrate it with the regenerative processor, and test it to ensure its efficiency and reliability inthe relevantenvironment. Focus shall be on the interfaces between the payload and components in the module, including also technologies used on ground, due to the high data ratesrequired. A fully functional Server in Space (SiS) module engineering module, capable of efficient on-board data processing and data storage, shall be designed, developedand tested. The SiS module shall demonstrateits capability to be integrated in future satcom digital processors and to be scaled to large data centres in space.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. original.description: The increase in small satellite missions has intensified the need for compliance to international space debris de-orbiting requirements. To meet these requirements CubeSat-class missions frequently rely on their primary On-Board Computer (OBC) and Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) to activate disposal mechanisms, however deployment and late-mission failures; such as battery degradation, bus freeze, or cyber compromise; can prevent successful disposal execution.This activity addresses this gap through the development of the Secure Autonomous Disposal Interface and Safety Module: a standardised, independent Disposal Trigger Module (DTM) compatible withCubeSat buses from 1U to 16U across a variety of disposal mechanisms. The DTM shall implement two autonomy levels of increasing complexity and prove resilient to spacecraft failures and cyberattacks. The project targets bring the technology to TRL6.

original.description: ESA CCI NG: The ESA Climate Change Initiative (CCI) Next Generation (NG) Essential Climate Variables (ECVs). This present procurement, referred to as CCI Next Generation (CCI-NG), is issued as part of the ESA Earth Action Programme. CCI-NG aims to perform the RDneeded to provide long-term, global satellite-based climate data records responding to the GCOS requirements for ECVs. In so doing,it provides the state-of-the-art EO-based climate information needed to monitor, understand and predict climate change and ensures that this capacity is available for transfer to sustainable operations, underpinning improvements in climate services.

original.description: Objective of the activity is to develop and test positioning-independent techniques for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) air interfaces.Targeted Improvements:Enable positioning independency for ground NTN terminals.Description: The development of a positioning-independent air-interface is deemed essential for future 6G NTN. Conventional 5G NTN terminals rely heavily on GNSS for positioning andtiming information, which means a terminal with no or poor GNSS reception cannot use NTN technology. Moreover, GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing and jamming,which can compromise the reliability and security of the communication links. By developing positioning-independent techniques, NTN terminals can operate without relying onGNSS or other positioning systems / sensors, enabling indoor coverage which is one of the goals in 6G for NTN as defined in the 3GPP roadmap. This feature is also crucialfor maintaining reliable communication in various scenarios, including critical infrastructure and emergency response. Positioning-independent modems can then operate inenvironments where positioning signals are weak or unavailable, such as indoors, urban canyons, or remote areas. This flexibility enhances the overall coverage and reliabilityof NTN services.This activity will explore the use of alternative techniques and protocols enabling a positioning-independent NTN air interface. Techniques and protocols shall be implementedin a modem prototype and evaluated in a real-time testbed possibly based on open radio stack.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl.
